root.name: Grünfeld Defense: Russian Variation, Accelerated Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 g6 3. Nc3 d5 4. Qb3

overview: White puts the queen on b3 to pressure d5 and prepare cxd5, instead of the exchange with e4. The main Russian System runs 4.Nf3 Bg7 5.Qb3 dxc4 6.Qxc4 O-O 7.e4, and Black responds with ...a6, ...b5 and ...Bg4 or ...Na6, challenging the centre. White gets a big centre and Black strikes at it with pieces.

white_ideas.idea: Win the c4 pawn back with Qxc4 and build an e4/d4 centre
Use the queen on the c-file and attack d5 and b7

black_ideas.idea: Attack the white centre with ...Bg7, ...c5 and ...Nc6
Gain time against the queen with ...Na6 or ...Be6 and ...Nc6

typical_structures.structure: Grünfeld centre: White pawns d4/e4 against Black pieces and ...c5 break

character.notes: Concrete central fights with tactics on d4 and the long diagonal.

soundness.notes: A mainstream line for both sides.

structure.notes: Centre tension where White's pawns are targets of Black's pieces.

approach.notes: A mainstream White choice against the Grünfeld.

level.notes: Needs theory, and the plans against a big centre are hard.

sublines_that_differ.name: Main Russian System
sublines_that_differ.how: Same set-up by a more usual move order; the accelerated 4.Qb3 allows more Black options.

character.reason: Concrete central tactics against a big pawn centre.

gambit.reason: Any pawn is regained by force.

structure.reason: The centre is in tension between White's pawns and Black's pieces.

level.reason: Grünfeld theory is long and plans are hard.

plans.reason: Black lets White build the centre then attacks it from the g7 bishop.
